transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump is returning from his first ever face-to-face meeting with the presidents
of China and Russia, instead of briefing the public about it right after the talks in Shenzhen.
Trump has opted to wait, NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben says no diplomatic breakthroughs were announced,
but the president was notably friendly with his authoritarian counterparts.
Trump referred to Russian President Vladimir Putin as his friend and said that he and Chinese
leader Xi Jinping have a "outstanding personal relationship."
Both of those leaders are accused of human rights abuses.
In a statement after the meeting, the three said they agreed to talk in the future about
curbing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.
They also talked about the importance of "immunities of state officials" and agreed that the International
Criminal Court "must not abuse their jurisdiction."
The statement did not mention the wars in Iran or Ukraine.
Trump says that he plans a press conference Friday at noon.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
On Capitol Hill, Senate Majority Leader John Thune was asked if he's worried Trump may have
conceded too much about Ukraine during the talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
As far as I'm concerned, I'm with Ukraine.
And so I think that's going to be where most of my colleagues find themselves.
Meanwhile, Putin has vowed a painful retaliation for Ukraine's attacks on a bridge that connects
Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Russia illegally annexed Crimea in 2014, eight years before Putin's forces launched a full-scale
invasion of Ukraine.
Myanmar is now the first country the UN's highest court has found to be guilty of genocide.
The International Court of Justice accuses the Southeast Asian nation of violating the
rights of the Rohingya Muslim minority during a brutal military operation in Rakhine State
in 2017.
While the ICJ's ruling is legally binding, the court has no way to enforce it.
Shares in the AI giant Anthropic are now trading publicly on the Nasdaq.
The company staged the biggest IPO in history, raising more than $100 billion for the offering
in a private placement, and PR's John Ruich says the share price jumped when it hit the
market.
Anthropic started trading at $111.50, a whopping 34 percent higher than the IPO price, which
itself was higher than expected.
That points to strong demand for the maker of the clawed suite of AI models despite growing
concern among investors about an AI bubble.
Anthropic was founded to develop safe AI for the benefit of humanity, and CEO Dario Amade
says that won't change.
We will not bend to either business nor political pressure.
Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens
our resolve to do the right thing.
Anthropic competitor OpenAI is expected to list shares next year.
John Ruich, NPR News.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
The Dane County District Attorney in Wisconsin says a white police officer who fatally shot
a 38-year-old black man in Madison in July will not be criminally charged.
The shooting touched off protests for racial justice, but the prosecutor concluded the man's
shot, Coy Ruiz, pulled out a knife and resisted arrest, and that it was reasonable for the
officer, Kiel Battinger Peterson, to use deadly force.
JPMorgan Chase is disclosing that third-party vendors may have been targeted in a cyber
attack, but on exit says there were no disruptions to its own services.
One of the biggest entertainment products of all time is here.
Grand Theft Auto 6 has already made nearly $2 billion, and it's only been out for one
day.
NPR's James Mastromorino reports.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first game in the controversial crime video game series in 13
years.
Finally!
So excited.
GTA 6 takes place in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City.
Real-life buildings and streets appear in the game, while Miami itself has rebranded
as Vice City in a multimillion-dollar marketing campaign.
That's just a sliver of its estimated budget of around a billion dollars.
The investment is paying off.
The game's on track to earn more than $3 billion within its first week.
And this is only the beginning.
Experts project that Grand Theft Auto 6 will make billions of dollars for years to come.
James Mastromorino, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump returns from first in-person meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin, no breakthroughs announced
Senate Majority Leader John Thune says he is with Ukraine after Trump's talks with Putin and Xi
Putin vows painful retaliation for Ukrainian attack on bridge linking Russia to Crimea
UN top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya Muslim minority in 2017 operation
Anthropic shares debut on Nasdaq after record $100 billion IPO, jumping 34 percent
Dane County prosecutor declines charges against officer who fatally shot Coy Ruiz in Madison
JPMorgan Chase says third-party vendors may have been targeted in cyberattack, no service disruptions
Grand Theft Auto 6 earns nearly $2 billion in first day after long-awaited release
